html:
A UN-run vote on 11 February 1961 in the British trust territory of Cameroons, which chose between joining Nigeria and joining the newly independent Republic of Cameroon.

Independence on its own was not offered. The northern part voted to join Nigeria; the southern part, Southern Cameroons, voted to join Cameroon, and on 1 October 1961 the two became a federation with English and French as official languages. In 1972 Ahidjo ended the federation. Many English-speakers felt their schools, courts and voice were swallowed by the French-speaking majority, and the grievance grew into the Anglophone Crisis. See also the split of 1916.
sum: A UN-run vote on 11 February 1961 in the British trust territory of Cameroons, which chose between joining Nigeria and joining the newly independent Republic of Cameroon.
